# Unexpected weight changes

*Categories: Clinical knowledge > Internal medicine > Endocrinology > Basics of endocrinology and metabolism > Unexpected weight changes*

[Original Article Link](/library/2s0T8h)

---

## Summary

Weight changes can have primary causes (i.e., change of caloric intake or change of physical activity) and can be physiologic or pathological. Unexpected weight changes can have various secondary causes including weight loss due to <u>malignancy</u> or weight gain due to <u>hypothyroidism</u> and are always pathologic.




See “<u>Unintentional weight loss and malnutrition in adults</u>” for diagnosis and management of <u>unexpected weight loss</u>.

---

## Unexpected weight loss

<u>Unexpected weight loss</u> is the unintentional or involuntary decrease in body weight (i.e., without the use of certain drugs including <u>thyroxine</u> and <u>diuretics</u>, a decrease of calorie intake or an increase of physical activity) of > 5% of usual body weight over a time period of 6–12 consecutive months. It can be due to:




* <u>Endogenous</u> factors

* <u>Malignancy</u> (e.g., <u>lung cancer</u>, <u>colorectal cancer</u>)

* Endocrinopathies (e.g., <u>hyperthyroidism</u>, <u>hypocortisolism</u>, <u>diabetes mellitus</u>)

* Gastrointestinal conditions (e.g., <u>gastritis</u>, <u>celiac disease</u>, <u>Crohn disease</u>, <u>ulcerative colitis</u>)

* Conditions with organ failure (e.g., <u>COPD</u>, <u>renal failure</u>)

* Infectious diseases (e.g., <u>tuberculosis</u>, <u>HIV</u>)

* Inherited disorders (e.g., <u>cystic fibrosis</u>)

* Psychiatric conditions (e.g., <u>schizophrenia</u>, <u>bipolar disorder</u>, major <u>depression</u>)

* <u>Exogenous</u> factors: <u>substance abuse</u> (e.g., <u>nicotine addiction</u>, <u>amphetamines use disorder</u>, <u>cocaine</u> use disorders)





References:[[1]](/library/7qc4-W0)

---

## Unexpected weight gain

<u>Unexpected weight gain</u> is an unintended increase in body weight without an increase in calorie intake or a decrease in physical activity. Common causes of <u>unexpected weight gain</u> include:




* Endocrine changes

* ↑ <u>Cortisol</u> (associated with, e.g., <u>Cushing syndrome</u>, <u>stress</u>, <u>depression</u>, <u>anxiety</u>)

* ↑ <u>Ghrelin</u>/↓ <u>leptin</u> (associated with <u>insomnia</u>)

* ↑ <u>Insulin</u> (associated with <u>insulinoma</u>)

* ↓ <u>Thyroid hormones</u> (associated with, e.g., <u>Hashimoto thyroiditis</u>, <u>iodine deficiency</u>)

* ↓ <u>Growth hormone</u> (associated with, e.g., infection, <u>brain tumors</u>)

* ↑/↓ <u>Estrogen</u> (associated with, e.g., <u>polycystic ovary syndrome</u>, <u>pregnancy</u>, <u>premenopause</u>)

* <u>Pregnancy</u>

* <u>Premenopause</u>

* Water retention

* <u>Ascites</u>

* <u>Congestive heart failure</u>

* <u>Pulmonary edema</u>

* Medication

* <u>Antidepressants</u> (e.g., <u>mirtazapine</u>)

* <u>Corticosteroids</u> (e.g., <u>prednisone</u>)

* <u>Antipsychotics</u> (e.g., <u>risperidone</u>)

* <u>Beta blockers</u> (e.g., <u>labetalol</u>)

* <u>Insulin</u>

* <u>Antithyroid drugs</u> (e.g., <u>methimazole</u>)





References:[[2]](/library/nqc7_W0)
